wave: CORRECTNESS -- a target repository with no `.atlas` directory at all crashed every CLI entry point instead of producing a typed not-ready report
wave_title: `adapter::audit_docs` called `Path::canonicalize()` unconditionally on the `.atlas` root it was given. For a repository that already has an (even empty) `.atlas` directory this is fine; for a repository that has never been admitted into Atlas at all -- no `.atlas` directory whatsoever, arguably the single most common real first-time input -- `canonicalize()` fails with a raw `io::ErrorKind::NotFound`, propagated by `?` through `audit_docs` -> `systemize`/`code_analyze`/`graph`/`docs_audit`/`work_prepare` -> `main`, which prints only the bare OS message ('atlas-systemizer: No such file or directory (os error 2)') with no path and no explanation, and exits nonzero. Every other 'declared but not present' fact in this codebase (a missing Cargo.lock -> `DependencyClosureState::NotApplicable`, a missing declared source root -> rejected/recorded not walked, a missing individual required doc -> a `required_control_docs_missing` entry) is reported explicitly and non-fatally; a completely absent `.atlas` directory was the one case still treated as a fatal, contextless OS error instead of the same kind of typed fact.

generation_model.G_n: 311fdc84e7 (docs(roadmap): correct R4.9-R4.11 status, understated by three dimensions) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Adversarial falsification of this session's own recently-hardened capabilities found no new gap in the identity-key collision class (systematically re-swept; every remaining unescaped `format!` join has either a single free field or a fixed-charset syn-lexer-derived field, both provably non-collidable) or in dependency-closure/reproducibility (confirmed byte-identical `systemize` output across two runs of the real repository). Pivoted to a fresh scenario category from the standing loop's own list -- 'malformed/hostile inputs' -- and constructed a minimal adversarial Rust source file (closures, `dyn Trait` dynamic dispatch, `async`/`.await`, generics) plus, separately, a syntactically malformed Rust file, each in a freshly-`git init`'d scratch repository with no `.atlas` directory (deliberately not replicating the earlier `adversarial_repo` scratch, which had accidentally been given an empty `.atlas` directory at construction time). Both `code analyze` invocations failed identically with 'No such file or directory (os error 2)', regardless of whether the Rust source was well-formed or malformed -- isolating the trigger to the *absence of `.atlas` itself*, not to anything about the Rust content being analyzed. Confirmed by toggling only the presence of an empty `.atlas` directory on the same scratch repository: present -> exit 0; absent -> the crash; created afterward on the same repo -> exit 0 again.

priority_classification: correctness (priority 1) -- every CLI entry point that reports engineering truth (`systemize`, `code analyze`, `graph`, `docs audit`, `work prepare`) crashed with an unhandled, contextless OS error instead of producing the typed report the architecture is designed to always produce, for what is very plausibly the single most common first-time real-world input: a repository Atlas has never been pointed at before.

design_decisions.question: Where to fix it: at `audit_docs` itself, or have every caller check `.atlas` existence first?
design_decisions.decision: Fix inside `audit_docs` -- the one shared function every entry point already calls, and the one place that actually needs the existence check to decide whether to call `canonicalize()`/`visit_docs` at all. A caller-side check would need to be duplicated at every one of the (currently five) call sites and would still leave the function itself unsafe to call directly (e.g. from a future caller, or a test) against a missing root.

design_decisions.question: Report a distinct new state (e.g. a `NotAdmitted` variant) or reuse the existing `DocsReport` shape with `gate_ready: false` and every required doc listed as missing?
design_decisions.decision: Reuse the existing shape -- a completely absent `.atlas` directory is observationally identical, from every downstream consumer's point of view, to an `.atlas` directory that exists but is missing every single required control document: `gate_ready` must be `false` either way, and `required_control_docs_missing` should legitimately list all of them either way. Inventing a new state would be a second way to express the same fact the existing `required_control_docs_missing`/`gate_ready` fields already express, violating this session's own 'avoid duplicate semantic concepts' discipline -- and would require every consumer of `DocsReport` to learn a new case for no added information.

design_decisions.question: Extract the required-docs list into a named constant, or leave the check's list as a second inline copy?
design_decisions.decision: Extract to a shared `const REQUIRED_CONTROL_DOCS`, used by both the early 'not a directory' report and the real walk -- a second inline copy of the same 20-path list would be exactly the kind of silent-drift risk this session already fixed once for BUILD coverage promotion (`code_analyze`'s own coverage disagreeing with `dependency_closure`) and once for the roadmap-vs-code status mismatch: two lists that are supposed to mean the same thing but are free to drift apart because nothing forces them to agree.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: `audit_docs` (and therefore `systemize`, `code_analyze`, `graph`, `docs audit`, `work prepare`) no longer raises a raw, contextless `io::Error` when given a root whose `.atlas` directory does not exist at all; it returns the same typed, non-fatal `DocsReport` shape (`gate_ready: false`, all 20 required control docs listed in `required_control_docs_missing`, `documents_total: 0`) that an existing-but-incomplete `.atlas` directory already produces, and every real CLI entry point exits cleanly (or, for `docs audit`, with its own pre-existing intentional nonzero-on-gate-not-ready convention -- never a crash) instead of terminating with an opaque OS error.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: New falsification-first regression test `adapter::tests::a_completely_missing_atlas_directory_is_reported_not_fatal`: constructs a real scratch directory with no `.atlas` subdirectory, confirmed to fail with the exact claimed `io::ErrorKind::NotFound` against the unfixed code (test output captured: `Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: "No such file or directory" }`), then confirmed to pass (`gate_ready: false`, `documents_total: 0`, `required_control_docs_missing` non-empty) against the fixed code.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Real, rebuilt `atlas-systemizer` binary invoked against two independently-constructed scratch repositories with no `.atlas` directory (one with adversarial Rust source, one with syntactically malformed Rust source) across all five real subcommands (`systemize`, `code analyze`, `graph`, `docs audit`, `check`, `parse`) -- all previously crashed identically with 'No such file or directory (os error 2)'; all now either exit 0 with a full typed report, or (`docs audit` only) exit nonzero carrying its own pre-existing, correctly-formed `gate_ready: false` report body (a pre-existing, unrelated linter-style convention, not a crash). The real repository's own `systemize`/`cargo test --workspace` output was re-verified byte-for-byte unaffected by this change (still `coding_admission.allowed: true`, zero blockers; 460 tests passing, up from 459).

implementation.adapter/src/lib.rs: New `const REQUIRED_CONTROL_DOCS: [&str; 20]` hoisted out of `audit_docs`'s body. `audit_docs` now checks `root.is_dir()` before calling `canonicalize()`; when false, returns an explicit not-ready `DocsReport` instead of propagating the `io::Error` `canonicalize()`/`fs::read_dir` would otherwise raise. New regression test `a_completely_missing_atlas_directory_is_reported_not_fatal`.

adversarial_and_falsification_coverage: a_completely_missing_atlas_directory_is_reported_not_fatal -- real scratch directory, no `.atlas` subdirectory at all, falsification-first (confirmed to fail with the exact claimed io::Error against the unfixed code before the fix was written)

real CLI verification (rebuilt binary) across systemize/code-analyze/graph/docs-audit/check/parse, two independently-constructed scratch repositories (adversarial closures+dyn-dispatch+async+generics source, and separately malformed/syntactically-invalid Rust source) -- isolates the trigger to `.atlas` absence, not to anything about the Rust content itself
toggle test on a single scratch repository: `.atlas` absent -> crash; `.atlas` created (even empty) -> exit 0 -- confirms the fix's precise boundary condition

full workspace re-run (cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace) and a fresh `systemize` run against the real Atlas-Studio repository itself, confirming zero regression to any existing gate, blocker, or test

recensus_scope_after_promotion: no prior CLOSED/EXTINCT conclusion depended on this crash existing or not existing, so no external conclusion requires reopening -- this closes a previously-unobserved crash path, not a previously-verified-safe one

the same 'declared-but-absent is a fact, not a crash' discipline this fix applies to `.atlas` is the same discipline already applied this session to a missing Cargo.lock (`DependencyClosureState::NotApplicable`) and a missing declared source root (rejected/recorded, not a crash) -- this generation closes the one remaining place that discipline had not yet reached

this generation's own adversarial-scenario-construction method (freshly `git init`'d scratch repos with genuinely nothing pre-created, rather than reusing an earlier scratch fixture that happened to already have scaffolding) is itself worth carrying into future generations: the earlier `adversarial_repo` fixture's accidental empty `.atlas` directory had silently masked this exact gap from being found sooner
overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. A target repository with no `.atlas` directory at all -- the single most common real first-time input -- previously crashed every CLI entry point with a raw, contextless OS error; it now produces the same typed, explicit, non-fatal `DocsReport` an existing-but-incomplete `.atlas` directory already produces, verified with a falsification-first regression test and real end-to-end CLI runs across five subcommands and two independent adversarial scratch repositories, with zero regression to the real repository's own state or any existing test.
